/-!
# Erdős Problem 476

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/476](https://www.erdosproblems.com/476)
- [Er65b] Erdős, Paul, *Some recent advances and current problems in number theory*. Lectures on
  Modern Mathematics, Vol. III (1965), 196-244.
- [ErGr80] Erdős, P. and Graham, R., *Old and new problems and results in combinatorial number
  theory*. Monographies de L'Enseignement Mathematique (1980).
- [Gu04] Guy, Richard K., *Unsolved problems in number theory*. (2004), xviii+437.
- [dSHa94] Dias da Silva, J. A. and Hamidoune, Y. O., *Cyclic spaces for Grassmann
  derivatives and additive theory*. Bull. London Math. Soc. (1994), 140-146.
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Erdos476

/--
Let $A\subseteq \mathbb{F}_p$. Let
$$
A\hat{+}A = \{ a+b : a\neq b \in A\}.
$$
Is it true that
$$
\lvert A\hat{+}A\rvert \geq \min(2\lvert A\rvert-3,p)?
$$

This is the Erdős-Heilbronn inequality, proved by Dias da Silva and Hamidoune.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 11, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/main/src/v4.29.1/ErdosProblems/Erdos476.lean"]
theorem erdos_476 : answer(True) ↔
    ∀ p : ℕ, Fact p.Prime → ∀ A : Finset (ZMod p),
      A.restrictedSumset.card ≥ min (2 * A.card - 3) p := by
  sorry

end Erdos476

reformulations.difference: The source's bound $\min(2|A|-3,p)$ is computed in ℕ as `min (2 * A.card - 3) p`, with truncated subtraction. `A` ranges over every `Finset (ZMod p)`, including the empty set and singletons, whereas the literature (e.g. Wikipedia) assumes A is nonempty. Primality is an explicit `Fact p.Prime →` hypothesis rather than an instance.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For |A| ≥ 2 we have 2|A| − 3 ≥ 1, so no truncation occurs and the bounds agree exactly. For |A| ≤ 1 the source's bound 2|A| − 3 is −3 or −1, so the inequality holds trivially. The Lean bound becomes min(0, p) = 0, which also holds trivially. `Fact p.Prime` is definitionally a wrapper for `p.Prime`. `Finset.restrictedSumset A = A.offDiag.image (·.1 + ·.2)` is exactly {a+b : a, b ∈ A, a ≠ b}. I proved in a scratch file, for every p and A, that the ℕ inequality is equivalent to the ℤ inequality `(#A.restrictedSumset : ℤ) ≥ min (2*(#A : ℤ) - 3) p`; the proof is by cases and `omega`. I also proved that the whole statement is equivalent to the integer form quantified over `p.Prime`.

sources_consulted: https://www.erdosproblems.com/476 (live site returned a Cloudflare challenge; read via http://web.archive.org/web/20260824202208/https://www.erdosproblems.com/476)
https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Restricted_sumset&action=raw (Erdős–Heilbronn conjecture section; Dias da Silva–Hamidoune, Bull. LMS 26 (1994) 140–146)
review.notes:
What I checked for `Erdos476.erdos_476`, the file's only declaration:

- **Source.** The archived erdosproblems.com/476 page asks: "Let A ⊆ F_p. Let A+^A = {a+b : a≠b ∈ A}. Is it true that |A+^A| ≥ min(2|A|−3, p)?" Its status is "PROVED (LEAN)": "Solved in the affirmative by da Silva and Hamidoune [dSHa94]." The Lean quantifies over all primes p and all `A : Finset (ZMod p)`. `Finset.restrictedSumset` (FormalConjecturesForMathlib/Combinatorics/Additive/RestrictedSumset.lean) is `S.offDiag.image (fun p => p.1 + p.2)`, and `mem_offDiag` gives x.1 ∈ S ∧ x.2 ∈ S ∧ x.1 ≠ x.2. So the definition is exactly the source's set.
- **Answer and status.** `answer(True)` has the right polarity for an affirmative answer. `research solved` and `formal_proof using lean4` match the source's status, so there is no status issue.
- **Small cases.** Evaluating every subset of ZMod p for p = 2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13 gives 0 violations. Equality is attained often (e.g. by arithmetic progressions: 114 subsets for p = 7), so the statement is not vacuous. It fails for the composite moduli 6 and 8, e.g. {0,2,4,6} ⊆ ZMod 8 gives |A+^A| = 4 < 5. So the primality hypothesis matters, and it is present.
- **Linked formal proof.** The plby/lean-proofs proof (Aristotle and Boris Alexeev, also quoted on the erdosproblems forum) states `(restrictedSumset A).card ≥ min (2 * A.card - 3) p` for `[Fact p.Prime]` and `A : Finset (ZMod p)`, using a product/filter definition. I proved in Lean that its definition equals `Finset.restrictedSumset`. I compiled its v4.33.0 ("latest") version against this repository's Mathlib v4.33.1 with the namespace renamed. From it I derived a theorem whose type is `type_of% @Erdos476.erdos_476`; `#print axioms` shows only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. The linked v4.29.1 version has the identical theorem statement; it differs only in Mathlib lemma renames.
- **Docstring.** It faithfully restates the source and correctly credits Dias da Silva and Hamidoune.

Optional, not a defect: the source's remark on Erdős's more general conjecture (sums of at most r distinct elements, bound min(r|A| − r² + 1, p)) is not formalized as a variant. I did not read the primary papers [Er65b], [ErGr80], [Gu04] and [dSHa94] themselves. The claim is settled by the erdosproblems.com statement and Wikipedia, which agree.

The checkout's modified `lakefile.toml` and untracked `run/` predate this review (timestamps 12:21); I changed nothing under /opt/formal-conjectures.
